subject: Follow-up: Pricing & cache hit assumptions (post-demo)
messages:

Subject: Follow-up: Pricing & cache hit assumptions (post-demo)

Hi Maria — great to meet earlier. Quick recap + the asks we agreed on so your procurement and product teams have the numbers they need. I pulled together the high-level pricing math we discussed and included an attachment (pricing_model_v2.pdf) with the same table.

Call recap (tl;dr):
- Product use case: in-app assistant for product pages (mix of repeated templates + free-form user Q&A).
- Key metrics you shared on the call: rough MAU 50k, ~3 sessions per active user / month, average session ~700 tokens (300 prompt / 400 completion).
- Target budget band you mentioned: $1k–$2k / month initially, with room to scale if unit economics look good.

Numbers to confirm (I used what you shared on the call):
- Gross monthly tokens = MAU * sessions * tokens_per_session = 50,000 * 3 * 700 = 105,000,000 tokens/month.
- Vendor list price (example model we demoed): $15 per 1M tokens (hosted inference).
  - Gross cost @ $15/1M = 105 * $15 = $1,575 / month.

Caching assumptions (this is the important lever):
- Prefix cache hit rate: how often does a request reuse a cached prefix/KV so we avoid re-computing the first N tokens? For product-page assistants we typically see a wide range depending on how templated prompts are.
- Example conservative / expected / optimistic hit rates: 20% / 40% / 60%.
- Effective billable tokens = gross_tokens * (1 - hit_rate).
  - 20% hit rate => effective = 84M => cost = 84 * $15 = $1,260
  - 40% hit rate => effective = 63M => cost = 63 * $15 = $945
  - 60% hit rate => effective = 42M => cost = 42 * $15 = $630

Implication: with a realistic 40% prefix-cache hit rate (we saw similar in a recent ecommerce customer with templated product prompts), your effective spend drops ~40% and the effective $/1M tokens also drops proportionally. In the example above net $/1M effective = $15 (list) * (effective/gross) so at 40% hit rate the effective unit is $9/1M tokens (63M effective for 105M gross => $945 / 63 = $15 list, but viewed vs gross it's ~$9 per 1M gross tokens).

Asks / next steps:
1) Can you confirm the MAU / sessions / avg tokens (or share a 7-14 day sample of logs)? even a small sample helps us produce a more accurate cache-hit estimate.
2) Share the set of prompt prefixes (product description templates, headers) — that will let our solutions engineer produce a predicted prefix cache hit distribution and expected savings.
3) If procurement wants a target effective $/1M (post-cache) number, what is the upper bound? you mentioned ~$10/1M gross earlier — is that correct?

I'll loop in Marcus (solutions engineering) to run a quick simulation on your sample traffic and Marissa (PEM) for whom to route procurement paperwork.

Thanks — happy to jump on another 30-min call this week to walk through the attachment and the cache math live.

Cheers,
Aditya Rao
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
aditya@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

Thanks Maria — this is perfect. Two quick things from our side while Marcus preps the simulation:
1) Mechanical example of how to think about "effective $/1M gross tokens":
   - List price (model L): $15 / 1M billable tokens
   - Gross tokens (what you measure in logs): 105M
   - If prefix cache hit = 40%, billable tokens = 63M -> list cost = 63 * $15 = $945/month
   - Effective cost relative to gross = $945 / 105 = $9 / 1M gross tokens (this is often the number procurement uses when comparing across vendors)

2) Prefix cache notes (how we estimate hit rate):
   - We group requests by stable prompt prefix (product template + system instruction).
   - For a prefix to have a cacheable hit you need frequent repetition and comparable completion length.
   - For Acme's product pages, we expect moderate repetition: recommended starting estimate = 30–50% hit rate. Marcus will produce a cadence distribution (how many prefixes, tail vs head) and a predicted bucketed hit-rate curve.

Next steps: Marcus — can you run the sim against a 7-day sample (anonymized) and return: projected gross vs billable tokens, bucketed hit-rate (head prefixes), and a recommended cache TTL for product pages? Marissa — I'll loop you in on procurement items and give procurement two contract options: hosted pay-as-you-go and a 3‑month reserved discount that bumps effective savings.

Aditya
